label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (updated 2 September) / DRC Ministry of Health — data as of 31 August 2026
contestNote: ECDC's tracker (updated 2 September, data as of 31 August) put DRC's confirmed toll at 6,186 cases and 3,007 deaths across 60 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces, an increase of 86 cases and 57 deaths from the 27 August figure. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 by its own Ministry of Health (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths) and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that the true case count may be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection captures an estimated 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026, months before the 15 May declaration.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly sixteenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,665 (August 13) → 4,945 (August 16) → 5,021 (August 18) → 5,290 (August 20) → 5,584 (August 23) → 5,713 (August 25) → 5,794 (August 27) → 6,041 (August 31) → 6,186 (August 31 report, published 2 September). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). WHO's 100-day assessment (24 August) recorded an average of nearly 90 new confirmed cases per day over the outbreak's first three months; Forbes (27 August) put the doubling time at roughly 2.2 weeks, faster than West Africa's 5.3 weeks.

source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 31 August 2026 (updated 2 September)
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 3,007 DRC + 2 Uganda = 3,009 total as of 31 August (ECDC tracker, updated 2 September), a crude CFR of roughly 48.6%. The toll passed 3,000 for the first time, having already surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history. WHO's 100-day review found roughly 60% of the ~260 weekly deaths recorded over the prior six weeks occurred in communities outside treatment centers. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said the outbreak was killing one person every 30 minutes as of 14 August.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,184 (August 13) → 2,325 (August 16) → 2,378 (August 18) → 2,516 (August 20) → 2,680 (August 23) → 2,744 (August 25) → 2,786 (August 27) → 2,911 (August 31) → 3,007 (August 31 report, published 2 September). 155-160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers; Forbes (27 August) cited 44-50 deaths (~29-32% CFR among HCWs). Over 40 healthcare workers killed and treatment centers/ambulances attacked per UN Secretary-General Guterres's 27 August Security Council briefing.

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~48.6% (DRC, crude, as of 31 Aug); ~69% in Beni health zone, North Kivu
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 31 August 2026 (updated 2 September)
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to 48.6% by 31 August as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones. Province-level variation is stark: Beni health zone in North Kivu has recorded 122 cases and 87 deaths, a roughly 69% fatality rate, and North Kivu province overall (868 cases / 589 deaths as of 31 August) sits near 68% — both well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — 70,000 Ervebo Doses Allocated, Phase 3 Trial Targeting Mid-September
value: 70,000 Ervebo doses released to DRC (20,000 for Phase 3 trial + 50,000 for frontline/health workers); human trial could begin by mid-September
source: WHO / Africa CDC / ICG / STAT News / Healio — 12–21 August 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. As of 21 August the human trial had not yet launched; WHO/DRC talks target a start by mid-September pending shipment, DRC regulatory/ethics approval and team training. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV (UK trial since 24 July) and Moderna's mRNA candidate (Canada Phase 1, early August) remain in earlier-stage animal/human safety trials and may be added later.
delta: 70,000-dose allocation approved 20 August; mid-September target date for Phase 3 launch reported 21 August
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, and a mid-September target launch are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (60 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 31 August 2026 (updated 2 September)
delta: Holding at 60 of 151 health zones as of 31 August, unchanged since 27-28 August — no new zones reported this week, though case counts within existing zones (notably Ituri and North Kivu) continue to climb
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of cases and deaths (5,065 cases / 2,305 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones as of 31 August) per WHO's 100-day review. North Kivu (868 cases / 589 deaths across 15 of 34 zones, including Biena and Manguredjipa), Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six affected provinces. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after the 42-day monitoring period. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic. DRC's Education Ministry began a nationwide 'differentiated' school year on 1 September, switching 18 of 138 educational subdivisions (13%, classified high-risk) to distance learning rather than closing schools outright.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~88% of identified contacts under active follow-up
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 31 August 2026 (updated 2 September)
delta: Coverage recovered to ~88% (31 August) from ~82.3% (27 August), back near the 90%+ containment threshold
deltaNote: ECDC's tracker reported active follow-up at 88% of identified contacts as of 31 August, up from 82.3% on 27 August. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border; a recalibrated Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69.3%, prompting a WHO/UNMISS preparedness mission to the border town of Ezo (27-28 August). Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following its outbreak-end declaration, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
